---
title: "Qi hourglass summary"
params:
  path_filenames: null              # One key_data CSV path per line (filenames.txt).
  path_summary: null
  analysis_id: null
  sample_prefix: "ptr_bmkgene"          # ID prefix only; does not identify modality.
  species: "ptr"
  metrics: !r c("spearman", "pearson", "Jensen-Shannon")
  comparisons: null                    # Infer labels; require every sample to have all.
  condition: null                      # Infer ONE condition; never pool conditions.
  adjust_method: "holm"
  alpha: 0.05
  bootstrap_interval_level: 0.90       # Diagnostic interval from saved bootstrap H.
  diagnostic_plots: true               # Individual effects and mean-H null histograms.
output:
  html_document:
    df_print: paged
---

# Joint evidence across Qi replicates

Within this **one dataset/modality**, combine independent biological replicates
with equal weights, separately for each metric and comparison:

\[
T_{\mathrm{obs}}=\operatorname{mean}_i H_i,\quad
T_b=\operatorname{mean}_i H_{ib},\quad
P=\frac{1+\sum_b I(T_b\ge T_{\mathrm{obs}})}{B+1}.
\]

The supplied example is `ptr_bmkgene_1-7`, comparison `Fusiform-Ray`. Labels are
read from the CSV, not replaced with `FuIP-Ray`. Keep distinct source datasets
and modalities in separate renders. The sample prefix is an ID namespace, not
proof of modality or biological independence; retain the prefix used upstream.
Bootstrap rows are not permutation draws; failed bootstrap iterations do not
prevent a summary when all requested permutations are present.

Sample-specific permutations must be independent across biological samples.
Spots, technical sections, metrics, and bootstrap draws are not additional
biological replicates. One Holm correction is applied to all metric × comparison
tests in this render (three tests for three metrics and one comparison).


**The statistic is unchanged:** both the observed statistic and every joint-null
statistic are arithmetic means across the same inputs. Null scores are **not**
concatenated across inputs. One row of `joint_null.csv` represents one joint
randomized configuration, not one input or one biological replicate. The null
standard deviation is not an estimate of between-plant variation.

Inference remains conditional on the specified upstream randomized-pseudotime
null and any trajectories, feature sets, and stage definitions held fixed.
A numerical audit does not establish exchangeability or validate those upstream
choices. Rejection is not a claim that every sample has an effect.

Input filenames are read from `params$path_filenames` (one CSV path per line).
The Snakemake rule writes an absolute-path manifest before rendering. For interactive
Rmd debugging, provide your own manifest and set `path_filenames`, `path_summary`,
and the required analysis identifiers through `params`.

## Setup

```{r Setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache = FALSE, error = FALSE)
fail <- function(...) stop(..., call. = FALSE)
text_vector <- function(x) as.character(unlist(x, use.names = FALSE))
scalar_text <- function(x) {
  is.character(x) && length(x) == 1L && !is.na(x) && nzchar(x)
}
require_columns <- function(d, required, label) {
  missing <- setdiff(required, names(d))
  if (length(missing)) fail(label, ": missing ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
}
constant_text <- function(d, fields, label) {
  for (nm in fields) {
    x <- as.character(d[[nm]])
    if (anyNA(x) || any(!nzchar(x)) || length(unique(x)) != 1L) {
      fail(label, ": expected one nonmissing ", nm, ".")
    }
    d[[nm]] <- x
  }
  d
}
# Preserve optional metadata instead of silently dropping it across files.
bind_fill <- function(xs) {
  fields <- Reduce(union, lapply(xs, names))
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(xs, function(x) {
    for (nm in setdiff(fields, names(x))) x[[nm]] <- NA
    x[, fields, drop = FALSE]
  }))
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out
}
key <- function(d) paste(d$sample_id, d$metric, d$comparison, sep = "\r")

read_filename_manifest <- function(path) {
  if (!scalar_text(path) || !file.exists(path)) {
    fail("Set params$path_filenames to an existing filenames.txt manifest.")
  }
  paths <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
  paths <- paths[nzchar(paths)]
  if (!length(paths)) fail("The filenames.txt manifest is empty: ", path)
  missing <- paths[!file.exists(paths)]
  if (length(missing)) {
    fail("Files listed in filenames.txt do not exist: ",
         paste(utils::head(missing, 5L), collapse = ", "))
  }
  paths <- normalizePath(paths, mustWork = TRUE)
  if (anyDuplicated(paths)) fail("Duplicate paths in filenames.txt: ", path)
  paths
}

files <- read_filename_manifest(params$path_filenames)
metrics_keep <- text_vector(params$metrics)
comparisons_keep <- text_vector(params$comparisons)
# The manifest is read directly in this notebook; no command-line parsing.
message("Loaded ", length(files), " key_data CSV files from: ",
        normalizePath(params$path_filenames, mustWork = TRUE))
if (!scalar_text(params$path_summary) || !scalar_text(params$analysis_id)) {
  fail("Set path_summary and analysis_id to nonempty strings.")
}
if (!length(metrics_keep) || anyNA(metrics_keep) || any(!nzchar(metrics_keep)) ||
    anyDuplicated(metrics_keep)) fail("Invalid metrics.")
if (anyNA(comparisons_keep) || any(!nzchar(comparisons_keep)) ||
    anyDuplicated(comparisons_keep)) fail("Invalid comparisons.")
if (!scalar_text(params$adjust_method) ||
    !params$adjust_method %in% stats::p.adjust.methods) fail("Invalid adjust_method.")
if (!is.numeric(params$alpha) || length(params$alpha) != 1L ||
    !is.finite(params$alpha) || params$alpha <= 0 || params$alpha >= 1) fail("Invalid alpha.")

outdir <- dirname(params$path_summary)
dir.create(outdir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
outdir <- normalizePath(outdir, mustWork = TRUE)
path_summary <- file.path(outdir, basename(params$path_summary))

read_base <- function(path, extra_fields) {
  d <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
  require_columns(d, c("sample_id", "metric", "comparison", "data_type",
                       "replicate_id", "seed", "H", "n_permutation", extra_fields), path)
  if (!nrow(d) || anyNA(d$data_type) ||
      any(!d$data_type %in% c("observed", "permutation", "bootstrap"))) {
    fail(path, ": invalid data_type.")
  }
  # Failed/missing bootstrap scores do not invalidate a complete permutation run.
  d <- d[d$data_type %in% c("observed", "permutation"), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(d)) fail(path, ": no observed/permutation rows.")
  d <- constant_text(d, c("sample_id", "metric", extra_fields), path)
  if (!d$metric[1] %in% metrics_keep) fail(path, ": unexpected metric.")
  if (anyNA(d$comparison) || any(!nzchar(d$comparison))) fail(path, ": missing comparison.")
  if (length(comparisons_keep)) d <- d[d$comparison %in% comparisons_keep, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(d)) fail(path, ": no requested comparison.")
  if (!is.numeric(d$H) || any(!is.finite(d$H))) fail(path, ": non-finite H.")
  if (!is.numeric(d$n_permutation) || any(!is.finite(d$n_permutation)) ||
      any(d$n_permutation < 1 | d$n_permutation != floor(d$n_permutation))) {
    fail(path, ": invalid n_permutation.")
  }
  d$source_file <- path
  d$source_md5 <- unname(tools::md5sum(path))
  d
}

validate_components <- function(scores, ids, comparisons) {
  expected <- expand.grid(sample_id = ids, metric = metrics_keep,
                          comparison = comparisons, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  observed <- scores[scores$data_type == "observed", , drop = FALSE]
  if (anyDuplicated(key(observed)) || !setequal(key(observed), key(expected)) ||
      !setequal(key(scores), key(expected))) {
    fail("Incomplete/duplicated sample-or-pair x metric x comparison grid.")
  }
  lapply(split(scores, key(scores)), function(d) {
    o <- d[d$data_type == "observed", , drop = FALSE]
    p <- d[d$data_type == "permutation", , drop = FALSE]
    label <- paste(o$sample_id, o$metric, o$comparison, sep = " / ")
    B <- unique(d$n_permutation)
    if (length(B) != 1L || B > .Machine$integer.max || nrow(p) != B) {
      fail(label, ": incomplete permutation count.")
    }
    if (anyNA(p$replicate_id) || any(!grepl("^Permutation-[1-9][0-9]*$", p$replicate_id))) {
      fail(label, ": invalid permutation IDs.")
    }
    p$iteration <- as.integer(sub("^Permutation-", "", p$replicate_id))
    if (anyNA(p$iteration) || anyDuplicated(p$iteration) ||
        !setequal(p$iteration, seq_len(B))) fail(label, ": incomplete/duplicate iteration IDs.")
    p <- p[order(p$iteration), , drop = FALSE]
    if (!is.numeric(p$seed) || any(!is.finite(p$seed)) || anyDuplicated(p$seed) ||
        any(p$seed != floor(p$seed)) || any(abs(p$seed) > .Machine$integer.max)) {
      fail(label, ": invalid/duplicate permutation seeds.")
    }
    if (all(c("Early", "Middle", "Late") %in% names(d))) {
      h <- pmin(d$Middle - d$Early, d$Middle - d$Late)
      if (any(!is.finite(h)) || any(abs(h - d$H) > 1e-8)) fail(label, ": inconsistent H.")
    }
    list(observed = o, permutation = p)
  })
}
component_summary <- function(components) {
  bind_fill(lapply(components, function(x) {
    o <- x$observed
    z <- o[, setdiff(names(o), c("data_type", "replicate_id", "seed")), drop = FALSE]
    names(z)[names(z) == "H"] <- "H_observed"
    z$n_null_ge_observed <- sum(x$permutation$H >= o$H)
    z$p_empirical <- (1 + z$n_null_ge_observed) / (1 + nrow(x$permutation))
    z
  }))
}
# A check for accidentally restarted schedules, not proof of stream independence.
check_distinct_schedules <- function(p, labels) {
  if (length(p) > 1L) for (i in 2:length(p)) for (j in seq_len(i - 1L)) {
    if (identical(as.numeric(p[[i]]$seed), as.numeric(p[[j]]$seed))) {
      fail("Identical seed schedules for independent units: ", labels[i], " / ", labels[j])
    }
  }
}
mean_test <- function(selected) {
  p <- lapply(selected, function(x) x$permutation)
  iterations <- p[[1]]$iteration
  if (!all(vapply(p, function(z) identical(z$iteration, iterations), logical(1)))) {
    fail("Different permutation ID sets within a joint test; complete the runs first.")
  }
  H <- vapply(selected, function(x) x$observed$H, numeric(1))
  T_null <- rowMeans(do.call(cbind, lapply(p, function(z) z$H)))
  T_obs <- mean(H)
  B <- length(T_null)
  k <- sum(T_null >= T_obs)
  list(H = H, iterations = iterations, null = T_null, mean_H = T_obs,
       B = B, k = k, p = (1 + k) / (B + 1))
}
# Independent arithmetic route: aggregate the original long table, not H_null.
audit_mean <- function(d, result) {
  o <- d[d$data_type == "observed", , drop = FALSE]
  p <- d[d$data_type == "permutation", , drop = FALSE]
  coverage <- table(p$replicate_id, p$sample_id)
  stopifnot(nrow(o) == length(result$H), !anyDuplicated(o$sample_id),
            setequal(o$sample_id, colnames(coverage)), all(coverage == 1L))
  reference <- aggregate(H ~ replicate_id, data = p, FUN = mean)
  reference$iteration <- as.integer(sub("^Permutation-", "", reference$replicate_id))
  reference <- reference[order(reference$iteration), , drop = FALSE]
  k <- sum(reference$H >= mean(o$H))
  delta <- max(abs(reference$H - result$null))
  stopifnot(identical(reference$iteration, result$iterations),
            length(reference$H) == result$B, k == result$k,
            abs(mean(o$H) - result$mean_H) < 1e-12, delta < 1e-12,
            abs((1 + k) / (1 + nrow(reference)) - result$p) < 1e-12)
  data.frame(audit_pass = TRUE, null_max_abs_difference = delta,
             p_recalculated = (1 + k) / (1 + nrow(reference)))
}

if (!is.numeric(params$bootstrap_interval_level) ||
    length(params$bootstrap_interval_level) != 1L ||
    !is.finite(params$bootstrap_interval_level) ||
    params$bootstrap_interval_level <= 0 || params$bootstrap_interval_level >= 1) {

if (!is.logical(params$diagnostic_plots) || length(params$diagnostic_plots) != 1L ||
    is.na(params$diagnostic_plots)) fail("diagnostic_plots must be TRUE or FALSE.")

# Read the saved bootstrap H values separately; NEVER put them in the null matrix.
add_component_diagnostics <- function(tab, group_columns, unit_column) {
  raw <- lapply(files, function(path) {
    read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
  })
  ids <- paste(tab$sample_id, tab$metric, tab$comparison, sep = "\r")
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ids))
  prob <- c((1 - params$bootstrap_interval_level) / 2,
            (1 + params$bootstrap_interval_level) / 2)
  diagnostics <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(tab)), function(i) {
    j <- match(tab$source_file[i], files)
    if (is.na(j)) fail("Diagnostic source file is absent from the input list.")
    d <- raw[[j]]
    same <- d$sample_id == tab$sample_id[i] & d$metric == tab$metric[i] &
      d$comparison == tab$comparison[i]
    o <- d[which(same & d$data_type == "observed"), , drop = FALSE]
    b <- d[which(same & d$data_type == "bootstrap"), , drop = FALSE]
    stopifnot(nrow(o) == 1L)
    if (nrow(b) && (anyNA(b$replicate_id) || any(!nzchar(b$replicate_id)) ||
                   anyDuplicated(b$replicate_id))) {
      fail(tab$sample_id[i], ": missing/duplicate bootstrap IDs.")
    }
    if (nrow(b) && !is.numeric(b$H)) fail("Non-numeric saved bootstrap H values.")
    h <- b$H[is.finite(b$H)]
    interval <- if (length(h) >= 2L) {
      unname(stats::quantile(h, probs = prob, type = 7))
    } else c(NA_real_, NA_real_)
    reported <- function(name) {
      if (!name %in% names(o)) return(NA_real_)
      value <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(o[[name]]))
      if (length(value) != 1L || !is.finite(value)) return(NA_real_)
      value
    }
    valid_reported <- reported("n_bootstrap_valid")
    metadata_ok <- if (is.na(valid_reported)) NA else valid_reported == length(h)
    data.frame(
      bootstrap_n_saved = nrow(b), bootstrap_n_finite = length(h),
      bootstrap_n_nonfinite = nrow(b) - length(h),
      bootstrap_n_requested_reported = reported("n_bootstrap_requested"),
      bootstrap_n_valid_reported = valid_reported,
      bootstrap_n_failed_reported = reported("n_bootstrap_failed"),
      bootstrap_metadata_ok = metadata_ok,
      bootstrap_status = if (!nrow(b)) "not_available" else if (length(h) < 2L) {
        "too_few_finite_draws"
      } else if (isFALSE(metadata_ok)) "metadata_mismatch" else "available",
      bootstrap_interval_level = params$bootstrap_interval_level,
      H_bootstrap_median = if (length(h)) stats::median(h) else NA_real_,
      H_bootstrap_lower = interval[1], H_bootstrap_upper = interval[2],
      uncertainty_scope = "within_input_resampling_not_between_individuals",
      row.names = NULL
    )
  })
  tab <- cbind(tab, do.call(rbind, diagnostics))
  if (any(tab$bootstrap_status == "metadata_mismatch")) {
    warning("Saved bootstrap counts differ from declared n_bootstrap_valid; inspect component diagnostics.",
            call. = FALSE)
  }
  # Descriptive influence check, not another hypothesis test. For inter-species
  # pairs, remove ALL rows involving the same randomized biological individual.
  tab$loo_unit <- as.character(tab[[unit_column]])
  tab$mean_H_without_unit <- NA_real_
  groups <- do.call(paste, c(tab[group_columns], sep = "\r"))
  for (index in split(seq_len(nrow(tab)), groups)) {
    for (i in index) {
      retained <- index[tab$loo_unit[index] != tab$loo_unit[i]]
      if (length(retained)) tab$mean_H_without_unit[i] <- mean(tab$H_observed[retained])
    }
  }
  tab
}

# Separate plots for each test; intervals are within-input bootstrap percentiles,
# not a confidence interval for the species-wide or population-average effect.
plot_component_effects <- function(tab, group_columns, label_columns) {
  old <- graphics::par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(graphics::par(old), add = TRUE)
  groups <- do.call(paste, c(tab[group_columns], sep = " | "))
  for (label in unique(groups)) {
    d <- tab[groups == label, , drop = FALSE]
    labels <- do.call(paste, c(d[label_columns], sep = " vs "))
    y <- rev(seq_len(nrow(d)))
    xr <- range(c(0, d$H_observed, d$H_bootstrap_lower, d$H_bootstrap_upper),
                finite = TRUE)
    padding <- max(diff(xr) * 0.08, 0.01)
    graphics::par(mar = c(4.2, 15, 3.5, 1))
    graphics::plot(d$H_observed, y, xlim = xr + c(-padding, padding),
                   ylim = c(0.5, nrow(d) + 0.5), pch = 19, yaxt = "n",
                   ylab = "", xlab = "Observed hourglass score H", main = label)
    graphics::axis(2, at = y, labels = labels, las = 1, cex.axis = 0.7)
    valid <- is.finite(d$H_bootstrap_lower) & is.finite(d$H_bootstrap_upper)
    graphics::segments(d$H_bootstrap_lower[valid], y[valid],
                       d$H_bootstrap_upper[valid], y[valid])
    graphics::abline(v = 0, lty = 3)
    graphics::mtext(sprintf("Bars: %.0f%% within-input bootstrap percentile intervals; no bar when unavailable",
                            100 * params$bootstrap_interval_level),
                    side = 1, line = 3, cex = 0.7)
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}
plot_mean_nulls <- function(summary, null, group_columns) {
  old <- graphics::par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(graphics::par(old), add = TRUE)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(summary))) {
    s <- summary[i, , drop = FALSE]
    keep <- rep(TRUE, nrow(null))
    for (nm in group_columns) keep <- keep & null[[nm]] == s[[nm]]
    x <- null$mean_H_null[keep]
    label <- paste(unlist(s[group_columns], use.names = FALSE), collapse = " | ")
    if (!length(x)) {
      message(label, ": no mean-H null; inspect p_method and p_group.")
      next
    }
    graphics::par(mar = c(4.5, 4.2, 4, 1))
    graphics::hist(x, breaks = "FD", xlim = range(c(x, s$mean_H)),
                   main = label, xlab = "Mean H across inputs in ONE joint permutation",
                   ylab = "Joint permutations")
    graphics::abline(v = s$mean_H, lwd = 2)
    graphics::mtext(sprintf("Observed mean H = %.4f; B = %d; exceedances = %d; P = %.4g; adjusted P = %.4g",
                            s$mean_H, s$n_joint_permutation, s$n_null_ge_observed,
                            s$p_joint, s$p_adjusted), side = 3, line = 0.3, cex = 0.7)
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

## Read and validate the key data

```{r Read key data}
inputs <- lapply(files, function(path) {
  d <- read_base(path, c("individual_id", "condition"))
  if (!startsWith(d$sample_id[1], paste0(params$sample_prefix, "_"))) {
    fail(path, ": sample_id does not start with sample_prefix + underscore.")
  }
  d$species <- sub("_.*$", "", d$sample_id)
  d$dataset <- params$sample_prefix
  if (d$species[1] != params$species) fail(path, ": unexpected species.")
  d
})
scores <- bind_fill(inputs)
if (!length(comparisons_keep)) comparisons_keep <- sort(unique(scores$comparison))
condition_keep <- unique(scores$condition)
if (length(condition_keep) != 1L ||
    (!is.null(params$condition) && condition_keep != params$condition)) {
  fail("Inputs must have one common condition, matching condition when specified.")
}
manifest <- unique(scores[c("source_file", "sample_id", "individual_id", "species", "metric")])
if (anyDuplicated(manifest[c("sample_id", "metric")])) fail("Duplicate sample/metric files.")
sample_metadata <- unique(manifest[c("sample_id", "individual_id", "species")])
if (anyDuplicated(sample_metadata$sample_id) || anyDuplicated(sample_metadata$individual_id)) {
  fail("Inconsistent metadata or repeated biological individual. Resolve replication first.")
}
components <- validate_components(scores, sample_metadata$sample_id, comparisons_keep)
sample_summary <- component_summary(components)
sample_summary$analysis_id <- params$analysis_id
sample_summary <- add_component_diagnostics(
  sample_summary, c("dataset", "metric", "comparison"), "individual_id"
)
sample_metadata
```

## Joint tests and independent numerical audit

The columns of the null matrix are biological samples. Rows are matching
permutation **iteration numbers**, not matched seeds or physical CSV row order.
Identical cross-sample seed schedules are rejected. These checks cannot verify
upstream shuffling, spatial exchangeability, or the biological sample design.

```{r Joint tests}
tests <- expand.grid(metric = metrics_keep, comparison = comparisons_keep,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
results <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(tests)), function(i) {
  test <- tests[i, , drop = FALSE]
  ids <- sample_metadata$sample_id
  lookup <- data.frame(sample_id = ids, metric = test$metric, comparison = test$comparison)
  selected <- components[key(lookup)]
  check_distinct_schedules(lapply(selected, function(x) x$permutation), ids)
  r <- mean_test(selected)
  meta <- data.frame(analysis_id = params$analysis_id, dataset = params$sample_prefix,
                     species = params$species, condition = condition_keep, test)
  summary <- cbind(meta, data.frame(
    n_samples = length(ids), samples = paste(ids, collapse = ";"),
    test_scope = if (length(ids) > 1L) "joint_samples" else "single_sample",
    p_method = if (length(ids) > 1L) "independent_sample_mean_permutation" else "single_sample_permutation",
    mean_H = r$mean_H, median_H = median(r$H), min_H = min(r$H), max_H = max(r$H),
    sd_H = if (length(r$H) > 1L) sd(r$H) else NA_real_,
    n_positive_H = sum(r$H > 0), fraction_positive_H = mean(r$H > 0),
    n_joint_permutation = r$B, n_null_ge_observed = r$k,
    null_mean_H = mean(r$null), null_sd_H = sd(r$null),
    null_min_H = min(r$null), null_max_H = max(r$null),
    observed_minus_null_mean = r$mean_H - mean(r$null),
    p_joint = r$p, p_resolution = 1 / (r$B + 1), at_minimum_resolution = r$k == 0L
  ))
  null <- cbind(meta[rep(1L, r$B), , drop = FALSE],
                data.frame(iteration = r$iterations, mean_H_null = r$null))
  d <- scores[scores$metric == test$metric & scores$comparison == test$comparison, , drop = FALSE]
  audit <- cbind(meta, audit_mean(d, r))
  list(summary = summary, null = null, audit = audit)
})
summary_results <- bind_fill(lapply(results, function(x) x$summary))
joint_null <- bind_fill(lapply(results, function(x) x$null))
audit <- bind_fill(lapply(results, function(x) x$audit))
```

## Multiple-testing correction and export

Adjust the raw joint P values **once across this report**, not across individual
samples or permutation iterations. This is a separate, declared validation
family from the in-house or inter-species analyses. To control a broader family,
collect its raw group P values and adjust that full vector instead.

```{r Adjust and save}
summary_results$p_adjusted <- p.adjust(summary_results$p_joint, method = params$adjust_method)
summary_results$adjust_method <- params$adjust_method
summary_results$n_tests_in_family <- nrow(summary_results)
summary_results$alpha <- params$alpha
summary_results$reject_joint_null <- summary_results$p_adjusted <= params$alpha
summary_results$hourglass_supported <- summary_results$reject_joint_null & summary_results$mean_H > 0
audit$p_adjusted_recalculated <- p.adjust(audit$p_recalculated, method = params$adjust_method)
stopifnot(all(abs(audit$p_adjusted_recalculated - summary_results$p_adjusted) < 1e-12))
write.csv(summary_results, path_summary, row.names = FALSE, na = "NA")
write.csv(sample_summary, sidecars[1], row.names = FALSE, na = "NA")
write.csv(joint_null, sidecars[2], row.names = FALSE, na = "NA")
write.csv(audit, sidecars[3], row.names = FALSE, na = "NA")
summary_results[c("dataset", "metric", "comparison", "n_samples", "test_scope",
                  "mean_H", "n_positive_H", "n_joint_permutation", "n_null_ge_observed",
                  "p_resolution", "p_joint", "p_adjusted", "hourglass_supported")]
```

A significant joint test rejects the combined randomized-pseudotime null; it
does not demonstrate an effect in every plant or estimate a population-average
true effect. With one sample, the raw joint P equals that sample's permutation P.
Zero exceedances produce the floor `1 / (B + 1)`, not a zero tail probability.


## Individual effects and uncertainty

Dots show **observed H**. Bars use the central `bootstrap_interval_level`
percentile interval of the **saved, finite bootstrap H values for that input**
(default 90%; type-7 quantiles). Missing bootstrap draws are reported, not replaced.
These are within-input resampling intervals, **not between-plant uncertainty**,
not species-level confidence intervals, and not evidence that spatial dependence
was handled upstream. Bootstrap intervals do not determine any permutation P value.
`bootstrap_n_*` columns distinguish saved, finite, and declared counts. Intervals
are conditional on usable draws; missing H values or failed resamples can affect
their interpretation. They do not by themselves establish nominal coverage.

`mean_H_without_unit` is a **descriptive** leave-one-unit-out mean, without a P value
or an additional significance flag. It is `NA` when no other unit remains.
Negative and nonsignificant observed scores are retained. Component P values are
unadjusted diagnostics, not the inputs to the group test.

```{r Sample summary}
sample_summary[c("sample_id", "individual_id", "metric", "comparison", "H_observed",
                 "H_bootstrap_lower", "H_bootstrap_upper", "bootstrap_n_finite",
                 "bootstrap_status", "mean_H_without_unit", "p_empirical")]
```

```{r Sample effect plots, fig.width=11, fig.height=6}
if (params$diagnostic_plots) {
  plot_component_effects(sample_summary, c("dataset", "metric", "comparison"), "sample_id")
}
```

## Joint-null distributions

The vertical line is the observed mean H. Histograms contain per-iteration
**means**, never pooled individual null scores.

```{r Joint null plots, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
if (params$diagnostic_plots) {
  plot_mean_nulls(summary_results, joint_null, c("dataset", "metric", "comparison"))
}
```
